findings.title: [P1] Define `renderError` before invoking it
findings.body: The new catch block calls `this.renderError(error)`, but a repository-wide search shows the only occurrence of `renderError` is this new call site — the class defines no such method and no mixin, prototype, or collaborator in the repo supplies it. Whenever `api.search` rejects (including the `AbortError` from a superseded search), the handler itself throws `TypeError: this.renderError is not a function`, so the error path is broken rather than handling the failure. Implement the method (or wire in the collaborator that provides it) so the new path actually works.

findings.title: [P1] Do not render errors for superseded searches
findings.body: `search` still begins with `this.active?.abort()`, so each new query aborts the previous in-flight request. With an abort-aware API (the reason the signal is passed), the aborted request rejects with `AbortError`, and the new catch now unconditionally calls `renderError` for it — routine cancellation is surfaced as a user-facing error on every superseded search (e.g. each keystroke in a typeahead), causing error-render churn and, when a stale rejection settles after a newer result renders, potentially overwriting the fresh result. Ignore abort errors and/or check that the controller is still current (`this.active.signal === signal`) before rendering.

findings.title: [P3] Add coverage for the rejected-search path
findings.body: The repository contains no tests, and the new behavior only executes when `api.search` rejects. Add a test that rejects the search promise (and one that aborts a superseded search) and asserts the intended rendering, so this newly introduced path does not regress unnoticed.
